newsitem.title: KENYA: Activity improves but Nairobi market depressed.
newsitem.headline: Activity improves but Nairobi market depressed.

text.p: Turnover at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) improved on Wednesday by about four million shillings but prices on key shares eased marginally, reflecting low demand in a moderately active market, brokers said.
The index went down 8.14 points to stand at 3,083.57. Turnover was posted at 22.941 million shillings on 538,393 shares from 18.597 million shillings traded on 440,903 shares.
Brokers said activity at the Nairobi bourse was boosted by Uchumi Supermarket which traded 100,000 shares on the three-day special board at a reserve price of 46.50.

Bourse officials said the market was fairly active with almost all the financials trading. Foreigners bought 88,200 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank (KCB) at between 75.50 and 80.50 from 83.50 and 16,500 shares of National Industrial Credit at 42 unchanged.
A senior broker said that despite the drop in price of Kenya Commercial Bank, at 78, the share was still doing very well.
"It's very funny how the spotlight has been on KCB for the last two weeks because generally other shares in the market have been quiet," he added.
Brokers said they believed that foreign demand in KCB had been sustained by refunds from large unfulfilled buying orders placed during the public share issue of October.

Another broker said that despite the increased activity in the financials, the prices were still holding out as many investors did not expect good bonus issues with the 1996 year-end company results compared to last year
On the corporate bond board, two deals were transacted at 101.9 at a total value of four million shillings.
Kenya Breweries traded at 50 unchanged, while oil concern Total Kenya closed at 65 from 64.
In the Agriculturals, Sasini Tea & Coffee traded at 63 from 60.50 and Rea Vipingo eased to 40 from 10.50.
